From c0e310188299358279fc27c88512f94db78991a6 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Date: Thu, 27 Feb 2020 08:57:04 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] drm/i915: Skip barriers inside waits

Attaching to the i915_active barrier is a two stage process, and a flush
is only effective when the barrier is activation. Thus it is possible
for us to see a barrier, and attempt to flush, only for our flush to
have no effect. As such, before attempting to activate signaling on the
fence we need to double check it is a fence!

Fixes: d13a31770077 ("drm/i915: Flush idle barriers when waiting")
Closes: https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/drm/intel/issues/1333
Signed-off-by: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Cc: Tvrtko Ursulin <tvrtko.ursulin@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Andi Shyti <andi.shyti@intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20200227085723.1961649-1-chris@chris-wilson.co.uk

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c
index 0b12d5023800..7b3d6c12ad61 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c
@@ -453,6 +453,9 @@ static void enable_signaling(struct i915_active_fence *active)
 {
 	struct dma_fence *fence;
 
+	if (unlikely(is_barrier(active)))
+		return;
+
 	fence = i915_active_fence_get(active);
 	if (!fence)
 		return;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_active.c`**
   - A new check was added at the beginning of the `enable_signaling` function to determine if the `active` object is a barrier using the `is_barrier(active)` function.
   - If the object is identified as a barrier, the function returns early, effectively skipping the signaling activation process for barriers.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `i915_active.c` addresses a specific issue related to the handling of barriers in the i915 driver. By adding a check to skip the signaling for barriers, the patch ensures that the flush operation is only attempted on valid fences, preventing ineffective flushes that could occur if a barrier is mistakenly processed as a fence. This change is directly related to the bug described in the patch, which aims to improve the robustness of the barrier handling during wait operations.

Here is the commit message:
drm/i915: Skip barriers inside waits

Attaching to the i915_active barrier is a two stage process, and a flush
is only effective when the barrier is activation. Thus it is possible
for us to see a barrier, and attempt to flush, only for our flush to
have no effect. As such, before attempting to activate signaling on the
fence we need to double check it is a fence!

Fixes: d13a31770077 ("drm/i915: Flush idle barriers when waiting")
Closes: https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/drm/intel/issues/1333
Signed-off-by: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Cc: Tvrtko Ursulin <tvrtko.ursulin@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Andi Shyti <andi.shyti@intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20200227085723.1961649-1-chris@chris-wilson.co.uk

Here is the root cause:
The bug arises from the incorrect handling of barriers in the i915 driver, where an attempt to flush a barrier could occur, leading to ineffective operations. The flush is only meaningful when the barrier is activated, and without proper checks, the system could mistakenly treat a barrier as a fence, resulting in unintended behavior during wait operations.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void enable_signaling(struct i915_active_fence *active)
 {
 	struct dma_fence *fence;
 
+	if (unlikely(is_barrier(active)))
+		return;
+
 	fence = i915_active_fence_get(active);
 	if (!fence)
 		return;
 
 	dma_fence_enable_sw_signaling(fence);
 	dma_fence_put(fence);
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
fence = i915_active_fence_get(active);
dma_fence_enable_sw_signaling(fence);
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the code attempts to retrieve a fence from the active barrier without checking if the active object is actually a barrier. If it is a barrier, the subsequent call to enable software signaling on the fence is ineffective, leading to unintended behavior during wait operations.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (unlikely(is_barrier(active)))
    return;
```
Reason:
This check ensures that if the active object is identified as a barrier, the function will return early, preventing any further operations on it. This avoids the ineffective flush operation and ensures that signaling is only attempted on valid fences, thus fixing the bug.
